title: Phillips' 107 Powers New Zealand to Record 259/7 and 87-Run Win Over India
excerpt: Glenn Phillips smashed 107 off 49 balls and Michael Bracewell 65 off 25 as New Zealand posted their highest-ever T20I total — and the highest against India — before Jacob Duffy's 4/23 sealed an 87-run win in the fourth T20I at Eden Park. India still lead the series 3-1.
body:
• New Zealand posted 259/7 at Eden Park — their highest-ever T20I total and the highest score ever made against India in the format, passing England's 257/3 in Southampton earlier this year.
  • Glenn Phillips hit 107 off 49 balls, his third T20I century, reached in 46 balls; Michael Bracewell smashed 65 off 25 in a 115-run fifth-wicket stand off just 40 balls.
  • Jacob Duffy took 4/23, including Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan in the first over, as India were restricted to 172 and lost by 87 runs.
  • India, who had already sealed the series, still lead 3-1 with one match to play; Arshdeep Singh became the first Indian to 150 T20I wickets in defeat.

Glenn Phillips' century and Jacob Duffy's four-wicket haul powered New Zealand to a huge 87-run win over India in the fourth T20I at Eden Park on Friday, as the hosts posted a record 259/7 and restricted India to 172 in the chase, according to IANS.

It is New Zealand's first win of the series. India had already taken an unassailable 3-0 lead, and the series now stands 3-1 with one match remaining.

A Record-Breaking Batting Display

Phillips smashed 107 from 49 balls, with six fours and 10 sixes, while Bracewell hit 65 from 25 deliveries. Their 115-run stand from 40 balls for the fifth wicket powered New Zealand to their highest T20I total, surpassing the 254/5 they made against Scotland four years ago, and the highest by any team against India, going past England's 257/3 in Southampton earlier this year, NewKerala reported.

Phillips brought up his third T20I century off 46 balls, having already scored an unbeaten 82 and 70 earlier in the series. He was dropped on 57 by Naman Dhir off Axar Patel — a reprieve that proved costly — and then hit four consecutive sixes in a 32-run 16th over off Nitish Kumar Reddy. New Zealand scored 85 runs in the final five overs. For India, Mayank Yadav was the pick of the bowlers with 3/48 on his return, while Arshdeep Singh completed 150 T20I wickets, the first Indian to reach the milestone.

Duffy Ends the Chase in the First Over

Chasing 260 — a total that would have been India's highest successful T20I chase — India never recovered from Duffy removing opener Sanju Samson for 4 and the returning Ishan Kishan for a duck in the first over. Abhishek Sharma made 27 and Shreyas Iyer 22, but India were 61/4 at the end of the powerplay after Matthew Fisher and Adam Milne struck.

Tilak Varma top-scored with a run-a-ball 35 and Naman Dhir made 28, but the required rate had climbed near 25 an over before the death overs. Duffy returned to dismiss Dhir, via a tag-team catch by Daryl Mitchell and Nathan Smith on the deep mid-wicket fence, and Arshdeep for a golden duck, finishing with 4/23. Mitchell Santner took 2/24.

What It Means for the Series

The result does not change who wins the series — India's 3-0 start had already settled that — but it changes the questions around it. India's bowlers, dominant in the first three matches, conceded their highest-ever T20I total, and the Phillips-Bracewell assault exposed the death bowling a game after the attack had looked settled. For New Zealand, Phillips is now the series' leading run-scorer with 276 runs in four innings at a strike rate of 189.

The fifth and final T20I closes the series, with India aiming to finish 4-1 and New Zealand playing to make it 3-2 and carry momentum into the ODI leg, which starts November 4.
